meta.title: dbms.pi

home.headline: Make your DB engine run your data fast and safely
home.description: A DBA and SQLP workbench for execution plans, statistics, and performance. schema.pi handles design and standards; dbms.pi is its partner on the engine side.

featDesc.connect: Register a schema.pi link token and check connection status
featDesc.sqlLab: Plan tree, warnings, comparison and anti-pattern checks against standard domains
featDesc.perf: Slow query Top-N, table/index health, capacity forecast, activity and locks
featDesc.monitor: Normal, warning, and danger for 14 signals, plus what to do and how to solve it at a glance
featDesc.drift: Compare schema.pi model and DDL history with the real catalog, measure index effect
featDesc.migration: Topological load order, chunks, checklist and verification SQL
featDesc.pipeline: Change-capture precheck and source→transform→target pipeline definitions
featDesc.analytics: KPI dashboard, 3-layer lake mapping and dataset catalog
featDesc.ops: Read-only diagnosis of parameters, roles, backup and replication DR
featDesc.learn: SQLP/DAP practice questions, tuning cases and DBMS comparison dictionary

migration.title: Data Migration (PiMig)
migration.intro: Computes the table load order from the relationships in your schema.pi design model, organizes chunk size, parallelism and the cutover checklist, and generates verification SQL you run yourself on source and target. This screen only plans and checks — it does not move data or read customer DB rows.
migration.needLink: Pick a schema.pi link above first. If you have none, register a token under 'Connect'.
migration.snapHint: The design at this moment (table, column and relationship names) is frozen as a snapshot. Create a new plan when the model changes.
migration.dropped: ({n} relationships without physical tables are excluded from ordering)
migration.optsHint: Parallelism is the number of tables loaded at the same time within a level. Chunk size is the commit unit (rows) the execution engine will use.
migration.orderHint: Topologically sorted by design relationships (not physical FKs) so parent tables come first. Tables in the same level do not depend on each other and can load in parallel.
migration.cycles: {n} circular group(s) — placed in the same level. Set their order manually and defer reference checks until after loading.
migration.selfRefs: Self-referencing (hierarchical) tables — load parent rows first within the table
migration.readyNeedAll: Check every item before marking the plan ready.

cdcHandoff.title: CDC handoff point
cdcHandoff.desc: Record a consistent source point before the initial load (PG LSN · Oracle/Tibero SCN · for polling, start time minus an overlap window), start CDC from it, and absorb duplicates in the handoff window with upserts.

valueConv.title: Value conversion
valueConv.desc: Rules are set for empty string = NULL, CHAR blank padding, NUMBER without precision → NUMERIC, DATE with time → TIMESTAMP, VARCHAR2 BYTE ↔ CHAR length, and LONG·RAW.

charset.title: Character set
charset.desc: Source character set (KO16MSWIN949, UTF8, …) is confirmed, with columns that overflow due to multibyte growth and isolation of unconvertible characters decided.

lob.title: LOB
lob.desc: CLOB·BLOB are streamed in chunks (size and memory limits) and verified by length + hash.

seqResync.title: Sequence resync
seqResync.desc: After loading, target sequences·identities are set to max(key)+1.

timezone.title: Time zone · system columns
timezone.desc: The interpretation time zone for values without one (e.g. Asia/Seoul) is set, modified-time triggers will not overwrite source timestamps during load, and creator/modifier substitution rules are set.

backpressure.title: Backpressure · target load
backpressure.desc: Reduce chunk size and parallelism on target lag, WAL growth or lock waits; build non-PK indexes after loading and run ANALYZE·VACUUM afterwards.

migration.verifyHint: Generates count, numeric column sum, duplicate key and key hash queries per table in load order. Run them yourself on source and target and compare (this screen does not execute them).
migration.noHashOracle: Oracle·Tibero hash functions and text rendering differ from PostgreSQL, so hash queries are omitted — compare counts, sums and duplicate keys.
migration.copyFail: Could not copy. Select the text and copy it manually.

engine.title: Execution·restart · rehearsal·rollback
engine.body: Actual migration execution (checkpoints, backpressure, error row isolation) and rehearsal, rollback and CDC start point recording will come after the worker agent security model (A10) is finalized. For now this covers planning, checks and verification SQL.

fix.AVAIL: Slow response or a recent restart — check the connection settings and DB server status.
fix.AVAIL_DOWN: Could not connect to the DB — check the connection settings and that the DB server is up.
fix.CONN_USE: {sess}/{max} sessions on this DB (not cluster-wide — other databases are excluded) — close idle connections or add a connection pooler (pgbouncer).
fix.URL: {n} checked URLs failing · max response {ms}ms — see the schema.pi monitor for the cause.
fix.LONG_QRY: A query has been running for {sec}s — review its plan and tune it, or have a DBA cancel it.
fix.IDLE_TX: A transaction has been idle for {sec}s — find the missing commit in the app and set a timeout.
fix.LOCK_WAIT: {n} sessions are waiting on locks — find the blocking session and end its transaction.
fix.CACHE_HIT: Cache hit rate {pct}% — look for full scans of large tables or review shared_buffers.
fix.XACT_ERR: Rollback rate {pct}%, {dlck} deadlocks — check the failing transactions and app error logs.
fix.SLOW_SQL: A query averages {ms} ms — tune the top queries by total time using their plans.
fix.STORAGE: The DB ({gb} GB) is near its limit (days left {days}) — clean up large tables or add capacity.
fix.VACUUM: {tbl} has many dead rows or stale statistics — review VACUUM (ANALYZE) and autovacuum settings.
fix.INDEX: {n} index findings (invalid, unused, full scans) — see the table & index health tab for the targets.
fix.BACKUP: WAL archiving is off or stalled — check archive_mode, archive_command and backup status.
fix.REPL: Replication lag {sec}s — check the standby status and the network.
fix.PGSS: pg_stat_statements is not installed, so slow SQL is unavailable — enable it with the SQL below (server restart required).

reason.CONN_DOWN: Not judged because the DB connection is down.
reason.NO_LIMIT: No size limit, so usage is not judged — add a DB size (MB) rule (>) to use it as the limit.
reason.RESET: Statistics were reset less than 7 days ago, so unused indexes are not judged.
reason.STANDBY: Not applicable on a standby server.
reason.GRANT: Missing privileges — grant the pg_monitor role to the connection account.

AVAIL.1: Check the connection status in Connections, and fix the connection settings (host, port, account) in schema.pi.
AVAIL.2: Check that the DB server is up and whether it restarted recently.
AVAIL.3: If it stays slow, check server load (CPU, disk) and the network.

CONN_USE.1: See session counts by user and state in the activity & locks tab.
CONN_USE.2: If many are idle, shrink the app pool or add a connection pooler.

URL.1: See the failing URLs and status codes in the schema.pi monitor.
URL.2: Check the app deployment and external dependencies.
URL.3: If it repeats, add a URL failure count (URL_FAIL_CNT) rule.

LONG_QRY.1: Find long-running queries and their users in the activity & locks tab.
LONG_QRY.2: Review the plan in SQL tuning and fix indexes or conditions.
LONG_QRY.3: If urgent, a DBA cancels it with pg_cancel_backend.

IDLE_TX.1: See the last query of idle-in-transaction sessions in the activity & locks tab.
IDLE_TX.2: Find the missing commit or rollback in the app code.

LOCK_WAIT.1: Find the blocking session (blocked_by) in the activity & locks tab.
LOCK_WAIT.2: End its transaction or have a DBA cancel it.
LOCK_WAIT.3: Fix batches or transaction order that hold the same rows for long.

CACHE_HIT.1: Find full scans of large tables in the slow query tab.
CACHE_HIT.2: Add the needed indexes to read fewer blocks.

XACT_ERR.1: Find rollback causes (constraint violations, timeouts) in app error logs.
XACT_ERR.2: If there are deadlocks, lock tables in a consistent order.
XACT_ERR.3: Check that retry logic is not inflating rollbacks.

SLOW_SQL.1: Pick the top queries by total time in the slow query tab.
SLOW_SQL.2: Review plans in SQL tuning and fix indexes or joins.
SLOW_SQL.3: After fixing, check that the mean time went down.

STORAGE.1: See the growth trend and estimated full date in the size trend tab.
STORAGE.2: Clean up large tables, indexes and old data.
STORAGE.3: If needed, add disk and update the limit rule.

VACUUM.1: See tables with many dead rows in the table & index health tab.
VACUUM.3: If it repeats, lower the autovacuum thresholds for that table.

INDEX.1: See invalid or unused indexes and full-scan tables in the table & index health tab.
INDEX.2: Rebuild invalid indexes; a DBA reviews and drops unused ones.
INDEX.3: Design indexes in SQL tuning for tables with many full scans.

BACKUP.1: See archive_mode and the last archive time in the backup & recovery tab.
BACKUP.2: If archiving fails, check archive_command and free space at the destination.
BACKUP.3: On a managed DB, check the backup settings of the provider.

REPL.1: See the state and lag of each standby in the replication & DR tab.
REPL.2: Check disk, CPU and network on the standby.
REPL.3: If it is not streaming, check the standby logs.

ops.title: DB Operations Safety
ops.intro: Read-only diagnosis of parameters, account privileges, backup and replication for the linked PostgreSQL connection. Nothing is changed; only verdict summaries are stored, never customer row data
ops.pickFirst: Select a link and connection above first
ops.readOnly: Diagnosis only reads (SELECT). Advice is a guide and depends on server memory, load and workload
ops.truncated: Too many objects — only the first 500 were checked
ops.paramsNote: Total server memory is unknown, so it is estimated from shared_buffers ≈ 25% of RAM. random_page_cost assumes SSD
ops.auditNote: Tables with RLS off and unused accounts will be checked once the link query supports them
ops.replNote: Baseline is Active-Standby (A-S) — one primary + standby. Replay lag ≥ 5s = warning, ≥ 60s = risk (measured RPO reference)

rules.sb_default: At the default (128MB). On a dedicated server about 25% of RAM is recommended
rules.wm_over: max_connections × work_mem exceeds estimated memory. Concurrent sorts risk out-of-memory
rules.wm_default: At the default (4MB). Large sorts and hashes may spill to disk
rules.mwm_default: At the default (64MB). VACUUM and index builds may be slow; consider 256MB or more
rules.av_off: autovacuum is off. High risk of table bloat and transaction ID wraparound
rules.conn_high: max_connections is high. Each connection uses memory; a pooler (PgBouncer etc.) is recommended
rules.lmd_off: Slow query logging is off (-1). Around 1000ms is recommended
rules.lmd_all: Every statement is logged (0). Heavy logging overhead
rules.st_off: No server-wide statement timeout (0). Set limits per role or application
rules.iit_off: No idle-in-transaction timeout (0). Can cause lock holding and bloat
rules.ckpt_short: Checkpoint interval is 5 minutes or less. Consider 10–15 minutes for write-heavy loads
rules.wal_minimal: wal_level=minimal makes PITR and replication impossible. Use replica or higher
rules.wal_ok: WAL level supports PITR and replication
rules.rpc_hdd: HDD default (4). For SSD, 1.1–2 is recommended
rules.super_many: Two or more superusers. Keep one for administration and grant only needed privileges to others
rules.bypass_rls: Non-superuser roles that bypass row-level security exist
rules.no_expiry: Login roles without a password expiry. Set VALID UNTIL for personal accounts
rules.expiry_ok: All login roles have an expiry
rules.public_grant: PUBLIC (every role) has table privileges. Write privileges are risky
rules.public_ok: No table privileges granted to PUBLIC
rules.arc_off: WAL archiving is off, so point-in-time recovery (PITR) is impossible
rules.arc_cmd_empty: archive_mode is on but archive_command and archive_library are empty
rules.arc_never: No WAL has been archived yet
rules.arc_stale: The last WAL archive is older than 24 hours
rules.arc_recent: WAL archived within the last 24 hours
rules.arc_failing: WAL archiving is currently failing. Check disk, permissions and target path
rules.repl_is_standby: This connection is a standby (recovery mode). Check lag from the primary connection
rules.repl_none: No standby connected. There is no disaster recovery (DR) setup
rules.repl_lag: A standby is lagging or not streaming

pgss.title: How to enable pg_stat_statements
pgss.body: Slow-query Top-N needs the pg_stat_statements extension. Run the statement below as a database admin. On Supabase, enable it under Database → Extensions
pgss.note: Self-hosted PostgreSQL also needs pg_stat_statements in shared_preload_libraries (postgresql.conf) and a restart. Table, index and size statistics work without it

pre.title: Source pre-check
pre.intro: For each table, checks change-time columns, soft-delete columns and the primary key to recommend a capture method (adapter), and checks WAL logical replication readiness. Read-only catalog and settings queries only.
pre.sum: {tables} tables · {noPk} without PK · {deleteUnseen} cannot capture deletes
pre.truncated: A catalog query hit the 500-row limit, so some tables may be missing. Specify a schema and check again.

ready.ok: WAL logical replication ready — tables with a PK can use LOGICAL
ready.no: WAL logical replication not ready — capture via polling or key comparison

reason.NO_PK: No primary key — changed rows cannot be identified

reason.FULL_RELOAD_ONLY: No PK or change-time column, so no incremental capture — add a PK

sqlLab.title: SQL Tuning Lab
sqlLab.intro: Pick a connection and enter SQL to see the execution plan as a tree, with slowdown causes (full scans, nested loops, large sorts) and SQL anti-patterns checked against schema.pi standard domains. Queries are never actually executed (no ANALYZE).
sqlLab.needLink: Select a link and connection above to view plans. The anti-pattern check works without a link.
sqlLab.sqlLabel: SQL (a single SELECT or WITH statement)
sqlLab.sqlPlaceholder: SELECT ord_id, ord_amt FROM ord WHERE cust_id = ...
sqlLab.saveNote: Constant values in the SQL and plan conditions are masked as ? when saved.

warn.SEQ_SCAN_LARGE: Full scan on {relation} (about {rows} rows) — consider an index on the filter columns.
warn.NESTED_LOOP_HIGH: Nested loop produces about {rows} rows — consider a hash or merge join, or an index on the join condition.
warn.SORT_SPILL: Sort size is about {kb}KB, above the default work_mem (4MB); it may spill to disk.

lint.title: SQL anti-pattern check
lint.domainsOff: Standard domains could not be loaded; checked with default column-suffix rules only.

codes.SELECT_STAR: SELECT * — select only the columns you need (extra I/O, no covering index).
codes.FUNC_ON_COLUMN: The filter column {column} is wrapped in a function or expression, so its index cannot be used — transform the constant instead.
codes.LEADING_WILDCARD: LIKE with a leading % cannot use a B-tree index — consider a pg_trgm GIN index.
codes.OR_DIFF_COLUMNS: Conditions on different columns are combined with OR — consider UNION ALL or per-column indexes.
codes.IMPLICIT_CAST: {column} is compared to a quoted number — match the column and constant types (implicit cast).
codes.NOT_IN_SUBQUERY: NOT IN (subquery) returns nothing when NULLs are present and is slow — use NOT EXISTS.
codes.NO_WHERE: No WHERE clause — on a large table this is a full scan (add a condition or LIMIT).
codes.DOMAIN_MISMATCH: {column} is a {expected} type by standard domain but is compared to a constant of another type — the implicit cast may prevent index use.
